open_points.subject: A01 rule 4 duplicate-submission semantics
open_points.text: `canonical_values` owns “A01 rules 1 and 4” but “Must not own where a value is stored”; rule 4 requires deciding that an identity already exists, returning its stored record unchanged, recording nothing, and not changing which version is current.
open_points.question: Which module owns the existence lookup and no-change semantics for resubmitted contracts, implementations, trial cases, flow versions and values, given that `canonical_values` cannot know `store` or the domain lifecycle?
options: Each domain-owning module applies rule 4 using atomic store capabilities
`store` owns the duplicate lookup and all no-change/current-selection behavior
`canonical_values` owns rule 4 and is allowed to depend on persistence
open_points.default_guess: Each domain-owning module owns its duplicate-submission behavior, while `canonical_values` only computes the identity and `store` performs the atomic lookup/change.

open_points.subject: randomly minted entity identifiers
open_points.text: “`trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.”
open_points.question: Which module owns the randomness source, identifier generation, collision check and retry for these records?
options: `store` mints every identifier atomically while inserting the record
Each record-owning module mints its own identifiers and asks `store` to detect collisions
A separate lower-level identifier provider owns random minting
open_points.default_guess: `store` mints and collision-checks the identifiers atomically with record creation.

open_points.subject: release dependency and sandbox-runtime pins
open_points.text: “The pinned Python dependencies and sandbox runtime of A20 rule 3 are a release artifact built and checked outside the running kernel.”
open_points.question: What module or explicitly named build component owns the exact dependency/runtime version record and verifies that the generated code and sandbox use it?
options: `data_provider` owns and exposes the release-version manifest
A named build/release component outside the runtime modules owns and verifies it
`sandbox` owns the runtime pin while the project packaging owns kernel dependency pins
open_points.default_guess: A named build/release component owns one checked version manifest consumed by the build and sandbox packaging.
